questions.text: सारा तथा तारा एक फर्म के साझेदार थे। 1 अप्रैल, 2023 को उनकी पूँजी क्रमशः ₹ 6,00,000 तथा ₹ 4,00,000 थी। 1 अक्टूबर, 2023 को तारा ने व्यक्तिगत उपयोग के लिए ₹ 1,00,000 का आहरण किया। साझेदारी संलेख के अनुसार पूँजी पर ब्याज 8% वार्षिक दर से देय था। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए तारा की पूँजी पर दिये गये ब्याज की राशि थी :
questions.text_english: Sara and Tara were partners in a firm. Their capitals as on 1st April, 2023 were ₹ 6,00,000 and ₹ 4,00,000 respectively. On 1st October, 2023, Tara withdrew ₹ 1,00,000 for personal use. According to the partnership deed, interest on capital was allowed @ 8% p.a. The amount of interest allowed on Tara's capital for the year ended 31st March, 2024 was:
questions.solution: The correct option is (A). Tara's interest on capital is calculated in two parts due to her withdrawal. For the first six months (April to September), interest is calculated on ₹ 4,00,000 at 8% p.a., which amounts to ₹ 16,000. For the next six months (October to March), interest is calculated on the reduced capital of ₹ 3,00,000 at 8% p.a., amounting to ₹ 12,000. The total interest allowed on her capital is therefore ₹ 28,000.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (A) है। तारा की पूँजी पर ब्याज की गणना दो भागों में की जाएगी। प्रथम छः माह (अप्रैल से सितम्बर) के लिए ₹ 4,00,000 पर 8% की दर से ब्याज ₹ 16,000 होगा। अगले छः माह (अक्टूबर से मार्च) के लिए घटी हुई पूँजी ₹ 3,00,000 पर 8% की दर से ब्याज ₹ 12,000 होगा। अतः उसकी पूँजी पर कुल देय ब्याज ₹ 28,000 होगा।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : फर्म के व्यवसाय को चलाने वाला प्रत्येक साझेदार फर्म के अन्य साझेदारों के लिए प्रमुख साझेदार तथा अभिकर्ता होता है।
कारण (R) : सभी साझेदारों के मध्य आपस में एक पारस्परिक एजेंसी का संबंध विद्यमान है।
निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Each partner carrying on the business of the firm is the principal as well as the agent for all the other partners of the firm.
Reason (R): There exists a relationship of mutual agency between all the partners.
Choose the correct option from the following:

options.A: दोनों अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) सही हैं तथा कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: दोनों अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is correct, but Reason (R) is incorrect.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is incorrect, but Reason (R) is correct.

questions.solution: The correct option is (A). Both the Assertion and the Reason are factually correct. The core principle of a partnership is mutual agency, which implies that every partner acts as both an agent (capable of binding other partners by their actions) and a principal (being bound by the actions of other partners). Hence, the Reason perfectly explains the Assertion.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (A) है। साझेदारी का मूल सिद्धांत पारस्परिक एजेंसी है, जिसका अर्थ है कि प्रत्येक साझेदार एक अभिकर्ता (जो अपने कार्यों से अन्य साझेदारों को बाध्य कर सकता है) और एक प्रमुख (जो दूसरों के कार्यों से बाध्य होता है) दोनों के रूप में कार्य करता है। अतः कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है।

sub_questions.text_english: Kartik, Inder and Lalit were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 4:3:2. With effect from 1st April, 2024, they decided to share profits and losses in the ratio of 2:3:4. For this purpose, the goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹ 1,80,000. The necessary journal entry to show the effect of the above will be:

options.A: Lalit's Capital A/c Dr. 40,000 To Kartik's Capital A/c 40,000
options.B: Kartik's Capital A/c Dr. 40,000 To Lalit's Capital A/c 40,000
options.C: Lalit's Capital A/c Dr. 1,80,000 To Kartik's Capital A/c 1,80,000
options.D: Kartik's Capital A/c Dr. 1,80,000 To Lalit's Capital A/c 1,80,000

options_english.A: Lalit's Capital A/c Dr. 40,000 To Kartik's Capital A/c 40,000
options_english.B: Kartik's Capital A/c Dr. 40,000 To Lalit's Capital A/c 40,000
options_english.C: Lalit's Capital A/c Dr. 1,80,000 To Kartik's Capital A/c 1,80,000
options_english.D: Kartik's Capital A/c Dr. 1,80,000 To Lalit's Capital A/c 1,80,000

sub_questions.solution: The correct option is (A). The old ratio is 4:3:2 and the new ratio is 2:3:4. Kartik's sacrifice is 4/9 - 2/9 = 2/9. Lalit's gain is 4/9 - 2/9 = 2/9. Inder has no change. The gaining partner (Lalit) must compensate the sacrificing partner (Kartik). The compensation amount is ₹ 1,80,000 multiplied by 2/9, which is ₹ 40,000. Hence, Lalit's Capital Account is debited and Kartik's Capital Account is credited with ₹ 40,000.

sub_questions.text: निधि, प्रणव तथा ईशु एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 5:4:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। 1 अप्रैल, 2024 से उन्होंने लाभों को 4:1:5 के अनुपात में बाँटने का निर्णय लिया। उस तिथि को लाभ-हानि खाते के नाम पक्ष में ₹ 4,00,000 का शेष था। उपरोक्त का प्रभाव दर्शाने के लिए आवश्यक रोजनामचा प्रविष्टि होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: Nidhi, Pranav and Ishu were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:4:1. With effect from 1st April, 2024, they decided to share profits and losses in the ratio of 4:1:5. On that date, there was a debit balance of ₹ 4,00,000 in the Profit and Loss Account. The necessary journal entry to show the effect of the above will be :

options.A: Ishu's Capital A/c Dr. 1,60,000 To Nidhi's Capital A/c 40,000, To Pranav's Capital A/c 1,20,000
options.B: Profit & Loss A/c Dr. 4,00,000 To Nidhi's Capital A/c 2,00,000, To Pranav's Capital A/c 1,60,000, To Ishu's Capital A/c 40,000
options.C: Nidhi's Capital A/c Dr. 2,00,000, Pranav's Capital A/c Dr. 1,60,000, Ishu's Capital A/c Dr. 40,000 To Profit & Loss A/c 4,00,000
options.D: Nidhi's Capital A/c Dr. 40,000, Pranav's Capital A/c Dr. 1,20,000 To Ishu's Capital A/c 1,60,000

options_english.A: Ishu's Capital A/c Dr. 1,60,000 To Nidhi's Capital A/c 40,000, To Pranav's Capital A/c 1,20,000
options_english.B: Profit & Loss A/c Dr. 4,00,000 To Nidhi's Capital A/c 2,00,000, To Pranav's Capital A/c 1,60,000, To Ishu's Capital A/c 40,000
options_english.C: Nidhi's Capital A/c Dr. 2,00,000, Pranav's Capital A/c Dr. 1,60,000, Ishu's Capital A/c Dr. 40,000 To Profit & Loss A/c 4,00,000
options_english.D: Nidhi's Capital A/c Dr. 40,000, Pranav's Capital A/c Dr. 1,20,000 To Ishu's Capital A/c 1,60,000

sub_questions.solution: The correct option is (C). A debit balance in the Profit and Loss Account signifies an accumulated loss. At the time of a change in the profit-sharing ratio, such accumulated losses are written off by debiting all partners' capital accounts in their old profit-sharing ratio (5:4:1). Thus, ₹ 4,00,000 is distributed as ₹ 2,00,000 to Nidhi, ₹ 1,60,000 to Pranav, and ₹ 40,000 to Ishu.

questions.text_english: Moksh and Pran were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 1:2. Their capitals were ₹ 5,00,000 and ₹ 3,00,000 respectively. They admitted Tushar as a new partner on 1st April, 2024 for 1/4th share in future profits. Tushar brought ₹ 4,00,000 as his share of capital. The goodwill of the firm on Tushar's admission will be :
questions.solution: The correct option is (B). Hidden goodwill is calculated by first determining the total capital of the new firm based on the incoming partner's share. Tushar brings ₹ 4,00,000 for a 1/4th share, so total capitalized value of the firm is ₹ 4,00,000 × 4 = ₹ 16,00,000. The actual total capital of all partners is ₹ 5,00,000 + ₹ 3,00,000 + ₹ 4,00,000 = ₹ 12,00,000. The hidden goodwill of the firm is ₹ 16,00,000 - ₹ 12,00,000 = ₹ 4,00,000.

questions.text: निर्देशकों द्वारा माँगे जाने से पूर्व अंशधारकों से प्राप्त अग्रिम धन राशि का लेखा :
questions.text_english: Money received in advance from the shareholders before it is actually called up by the directors is:

options.A: अग्रिम याचना खाते के जमा पक्ष में किया जाता है।
options.B: अग्रिम याचना खाते के नाम पक्ष में किया जाता है।
options.C: याचना खाते के जमा पक्ष में किया जाता है।
options.D: अदत्त याचना खाते के नाम पक्ष में किया जाता है।

options_english.A: credited to calls in advance account.
options_english.B: debited to calls in advance account.
options_english.D: debited to calls in arrears account.

questions.solution: The correct option is (A). When a company receives money from shareholders before the relevant calls are formally made by the board of directors, this excess amount represents a liability for the company until it becomes due. Therefore, it is credited to a separate account known as the 'Calls in Advance Account'.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (A) है। जब कम्पनी अंशधारकों से वह राशि प्राप्त कर लेती है जिसकी याचना निर्देशकों द्वारा अभी तक नहीं की गई है, तो यह राशि कम्पनी के लिए एक देयता होती है। अतः इसे एक अलग खाते में जमा (credit) किया जाता है जिसे 'अग्रिम याचना खाता' कहते हैं।

sub_questions.text: मिशा, सरिता तथा ईशा एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 3:2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। 1 अप्रैल, 2024 से उन्होंने निर्णय लिया कि वे लाभ-हानि को बराबर-बराबर बाँटेंगे। लाभ विभाजन अनुपात में परिवर्तन के कारण साझेदारों का अधिलाभ अथवा त्याग होगा :
sub_questions.text_english: Misha, Sarita and Isha were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2:1. With effect from 1st April 2024, they decided that they will share profits and losses equally. The gain or sacrifice by the partners due to change in profit sharing ratio will be:

options.A: मिशा का त्याग 1/6, ईशा का अधिलाभ 1/6
options.B: मिशा का अधिलाभ 1/6, ईशा का त्याग 1/6
options.C: मिशा का त्याग 1/6, सरिता का अधिलाभ 1/3, ईशा का त्याग 1/6
options.D: मिशा का त्याग 1/3, ईशा का अधिलाभ 1/3

options_english.C: Misha's sacrifice 1/6, Sarita's gain 1/3, Isha's sacrifice 1/6

sub_questions.solution: The correct option is (A). The old ratio is 3:2:1 (3/6, 2/6, 1/6). The new ratio is equal, i.e., 1:1:1 (2/6, 2/6, 2/6). We calculate the difference (Old Share - New Share): For Misha, it is 3/6 - 2/6 = +1/6 (Sacrifice). For Sarita, it is 2/6 - 2/6 = 0 (No change). For Isha, it is 1/6 - 2/6 = -1/6 (Gain). Thus, Misha sacrifices 1/6 and Isha gains 1/6.

sub_questions.text_english: Sia, Tisha and Aryan were partners sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 4:7:1. The firm closes its books on 31st March every year. Tisha died on 1st July, 2024. Sia and Aryan will acquire Tisha's share in which of the following ratio?
sub_questions.solution: The correct option is (B). The original profit-sharing ratio among Sia, Tisha, and Aryan was 4:7:1. Upon the death of Tisha, since no new profit-sharing ratio is agreed upon or given, it is assumed that the remaining partners will acquire the deceased partner's share in their existing relative profit-sharing ratio. The ratio between Sia and Aryan is 4:1.

questions.text: अनुज तथा कार्तिक एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 5:4 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। 1 अप्रैल, 2023 से आरम्भ कर 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष में प्रत्येक वैकल्पिक महीने के आरम्भ में अनुज ने ₹ 20,000 का आहरण किया। 6% वार्षिक दर से 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष में अनुज के आहरण पर ब्याज होगा :
questions.text_english: Anuj and Kartik were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:4. Anuj withdrew ₹ 20,000 in the beginning of every alternate month starting from 1st April, 2023 during the year ended 31st March, 2024. Interest on Anuj's drawings @ 6% p.a. for the year ended 31st March, 2024 will be :
questions.solution: The correct option is (C). Anuj withdraws ₹ 20,000 at the beginning of every alternate month. There are 6 alternate months in a year, so total drawings = ₹ 20,000 × 6 = ₹ 1,20,000. The average period for drawings made at the beginning of every alternate month is calculated as (Months left after first drawing + Months left after last drawing) / 2 = (12 + 2) / 2 = 7 months. The interest on drawings is calculated as: ₹ 1,20,000 × (6/100) × (7/12) = ₹ 4,200.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (C) है। अनुज प्रत्येक वैकल्पिक महीने के आरम्भ में ₹ 20,000 का आहरण करता है, इसलिए वर्ष में कुल 6 बार आहरण होंगे। कुल आहरण = ₹ 20,000 × 6 = ₹ 1,20,000. औसत अवधि = (प्रथम आहरण के बाद बचे माह + अंतिम आहरण के बाद बचे माह) / 2 = (12 + 2) / 2 = 7 माह। ब्याज की गणना = ₹ 1,20,000 × (6/100) × (7/12) = ₹ 4,200 होगी।

sub_questions.text_english: Vishesh, Manik and Amit were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:4:1. Amit retired on 31st March, 2024. Vishesh and Manik acquired Amit's share in the ratio of 2:3. The new profit sharing ratio between Vishesh and Manik after Amit's retirement will be :
sub_questions.solution: The correct option is (D). Amit's share is 1/10. Vishesh acquires 2/5th of 1/10 = 2/50. Manik acquires 3/5th of 1/10 = 3/50. Vishesh's new share = Old share (5/10) + Gained share (2/50) = 25/50 + 2/50 = 27/50. Manik's new share = Old share (4/10) + Gained share (3/50) = 20/50 + 3/50 = 23/50. Therefore, the new ratio is 27:23.

sub_questions.text: वर्षा, आर्यन तथा निमित एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 2:2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। वर्षा सेवा निवृत्त हो गयी तथा उसने अपने भाग का 1/3 भाग आर्यन के पक्ष में समर्पित किया तथा शेष भाग निमित के पक्ष में। आर्यन तथा निमित के मध्य नया लाभ विभाजन अनुपात होगा :
sub_questions.text_english: Varsha, Aryan and Nimit were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 2:2:1. Varsha retired and surrendered 1/3rd of her share in favour of Aryan and the remaining share in favour of Nimit. The new profit sharing ratio between Aryan and Nimit will be:
sub_questions.solution: The correct option is (B). Varsha's share is 2/5. Aryan gains 1/3rd of Varsha's share: (1/3) * (2/5) = 2/15. Nimit gains the remaining 2/3rd of Varsha's share: (2/3) * (2/5) = 4/15. Aryan's new share = Old share (2/5) + Gain (2/15) = (6+2)/15 = 8/15. Nimit's new share = Old share (1/5) + Gain (4/15) = (3+4)/15 = 7/15. The new profit-sharing ratio is 8:7.

questions.text: जब साझेदारों की पूँजी स्थायी होती है तो एक साझेदार द्वारा किये गये आहरणों का लेखा किया जाता है :
questions.text_english: When the partners' capitals are fixed, the drawings made by a partner are recorded on the :

options.A: साझेदार के पूँजी खाते के नाम पक्ष में
options.B: साझेदार के पूँजी खाते के जमा पक्ष में
options.C: साझेदार के चालू खाते के नाम पक्ष में
options.D: साझेदार के चालू खाते के जमा पक्ष में

options_english.A: Debit side of Partner's Capital Account.
options_english.B: Credit side of Partner's Capital Account.
options_english.C: Debit side of Partner's Current Account.
options_english.D: Credit side of Partner's Current Account.

questions.solution: The correct option is (C). Under the fixed capital method, two separate accounts are maintained for each partner: the Capital Account and the Current Account. Drawings out of profits made by a partner decrease their current balance, so they are debited to the respective Partner's Current Account.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (C) है। स्थायी पूँजी पद्धति के अंतर्गत प्रत्येक साझेदार के दो खाते (पूँजी खाता तथा चालू खाता) बनाए जाते हैं। लाभों में से किये गए आहरण साझेदार के चालू खाते के शेष को कम करते हैं, अतः इन्हें साझेदार के चालू खाते के नाम (Debit) पक्ष में लिखा जाता है।

questions.text: ₹ 10 प्रत्येक के 4,000 अंशों का हरण ₹ 2 प्रति अंश की दूसरी तथा अन्तिम याचना राशि का भुगतान न करने पर किया गया। इन अंशों के पुनः निर्गमन पर कम्पनी द्वारा आवश्यक रूप से एकत्रित की जाने वाली न्यूनतम राशि होगी :
questions.text_english: 4,000 shares of ₹ 10 each were forfeited for non-payment of second and final call money of ₹ 2 per share. The minimum amount that the company must collect at the time of reissue of these shares will be:
questions.solution: The correct option is (A). A company can issue forfeited shares at a discount, but the maximum permissible discount is the amount previously received (forfeited) on those shares. On 4,000 shares, ₹ 8 per share was received (as ₹ 2 was unpaid). Maximum discount allowed = 4,000 × ₹ 8 = ₹ 32,000. Minimum reissue amount = Total face value (₹ 40,000) - Maximum discount (₹ 32,000) = ₹ 8,000.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (A) है। कम्पनी हरण किए गए अंशों को बट्टे पर पुनः निर्गमित कर सकती है, लेकिन अधिकतम बट्टा वह राशि होती है जो उन अंशों पर पहले ही प्राप्त हो चुकी है। 4,000 अंशों पर ₹ 8 प्रति अंश (₹ 2 का भुगतान न होने के कारण) प्राप्त हो चुके थे। अधिकतम बट्टा = 4,000 × ₹ 8 = ₹ 32,000. अतः कम्पनी द्वारा एकत्रित की जाने वाली न्यूनतम राशि = कुल अंकित मूल्य (₹ 40,000) - अधिकतम बट्टा (₹ 32,000) = ₹ 8,000 होगी।

questions.text: 1 अप्रैल, 2023 को वीबी लिमिटेड ने ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 20,000, 13% ऋणपत्रों का निर्गमन 10% बट्टे पर किया जिनका शोधन 4 वर्षों के पश्चात 5% प्रीमियम पर किया जाएगा। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त होने वाले वर्ष के लिए ऋणपत्रों पर ब्याज की कुल राशि होगी :
questions.text_english: On 1st April 2023, Veebee Ltd. issued 20,000, 13% debentures of ₹ 100 each at a discount of 10% redeemable at a premium of 5% after 4 years. Total amount of interest on debentures for the year ending 31st March, 2024 will be:
questions.solution: The correct option is (B). Interest on debentures is always calculated on the nominal or face value of the issued debentures, regardless of whether they are issued at a discount or a premium. Face value of the issued debentures = 20,000 × ₹ 100 = ₹ 20,00,000. Interest for one full year (ending 31st March, 2024) at 13% = ₹ 20,00,000 × 13% = ₹ 2,60,000.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (B) है। ऋणपत्रों पर ब्याज की गणना हमेशा उनके अंकित मूल्य (Face Value) पर की जाती है, चाहे उनका निर्गमन बट्टे या प्रीमियम पर किया गया हो। ऋणपत्रों का कुल अंकित मूल्य = 20,000 × ₹ 100 = ₹ 20,00,000 है। 13% की दर से एक वर्ष का ब्याज = ₹ 20,00,000 × 13% = ₹ 2,60,000 होगा।

questions.text: आरुषि, विवान तथा मिताली एक फर्म के साझेदार थे। 31 मार्च, 2024 को फर्म का विघटन हो गया। उस तिथि को फर्म की पुस्तकों में ₹ 60,000 के देनदार तथा ₹ 3,000 संदिग्ध ऋणों के लिए प्रावधान विद्यमान था। ₹ 8,000 के देनदार डूब गये तथा शेष देनदारों से पूरी राशि वसूल हो गयी। देनदारों से वसूली गई राशि थी :
questions.text_english: Arushi, Vivaan and Mitali were partners in a firm. On 31st March 2024, the firm was dissolved. On that date the firm had debtors of ₹ 60,000 and provision for doubtful debts of ₹ 3,000 were existing in the books. Debtors of ₹ 8,000 proved bad and full amount was realised from the remaining debtors. The amount realised from debtors was:
questions.solution: The correct option is (C). At the time of dissolution, gross debtors of ₹ 60,000 are transferred to the debit side of the Realisation Account. When realizing assets, the gross book value of debtors is considered. Debtors worth ₹ 8,000 proved bad, so the remaining amount was fully realized. The realized amount is therefore ₹ 60,000 - ₹ 8,000 = ₹ 52,000. The provision of ₹ 3,000 transferred to the credit side of Realisation Account has no bearing on the cash realization.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (C) है। विघटन के समय ₹ 60,000 के कुल देनदारों को वसूली खाते के नाम (Debit) पक्ष में हस्तांतरित किया जाता है। वसूली गई राशि की गणना कुल देनदारों से होती है। ₹ 8,000 के देनदार डूब गए, अतः शेष देनदारों से प्राप्त राशि = ₹ 60,000 - ₹ 8,000 = ₹ 52,000 होगी। ₹ 3,00,000 का प्रावधान वसूली खाते में जमा कर दिया जाता है और उसका रोकड़ वसूली से कोई सीधा संबंध नहीं होता है।

questions.text: अश्मित, वीना तथा रोहन एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 3:2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। 31 मार्च, 2024 को वीना सेवा निवृत्त हो गयी। पुनर्मूल्यांकन, ख्याति, संचयों आदि से संबंधित सभी समायोजनों के पश्चात अश्मित, वीना तथा रोहन के पूँजी खातों में क्रमशः ₹ 2,00,000, ₹ 1,80,000 तथा ₹ 1,20,000 के जमा शेष थे। वीना को भुगतान अश्मित तथा रोहन द्वारा लाये गये रोकड़ के द्वारा इस प्रकार किया गया कि उनकी पूँजी उनके नये लाभ विभाजन अनुपात में हो जाये। अश्मित तथा रोहन की नयी पूँजी होगी :
questions.text_english: Ashmit, Veena and Rohan were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2:1. Veena retired on 31st March, 2024. The capital accounts of Ashmit, Veena and Rohan showed a credit balance of ₹ 2,00,000, ₹ 1,80,000 and ₹ 1,20,000 respectively after making all adjustments relating to revaluation, goodwill, reserves etc. Veena was paid in cash brought in by Ashmit and Rohan in such a way that their capitals were in proportion to their new profit sharing ratio. The new capitals of Ashmit and Rohan will be :
questions.solution: The correct option is (A). Since Veena retires from the 3:2:1 ratio, the new profit-sharing ratio between Ashmit and Rohan becomes 3:1. The total capital of the newly constituted firm equals the combined adjusted capitals of all partners before Veena's payout, as Ashmit and Rohan are bringing in cash equal to what is being paid out. Total Capital = ₹ 2,00,000 + ₹ 1,80,000 + ₹ 1,20,000 = ₹ 5,00,000. Distributing this in the new 3:1 ratio gives Ashmit: ₹ 5,00,000 × 3/4 = ₹ 3,75,000, and Rohan: ₹ 5,00,000 × 1/4 = ₹ 1,25,000.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (A) है। वीना के 3:2:1 अनुपात से सेवानिवृत्त होने पर अश्मित और रोहन का नया लाभ-हानि अनुपात 3:1 होगा। नई फर्म की कुल पूँजी तीनों साझेदारों की समायोजित पूँजी के योग के बराबर होगी, क्योंकि वीना को देय राशि अश्मित और रोहन नगद ला रहे हैं। कुल पूँजी = ₹ 2,00,000 + ₹ 1,80,000 + ₹ 1,20,000 = ₹ 5,00,000. इसे 3:1 के अनुपात में बाँटने पर अश्मित की पूँजी = ₹ 5,00,000 × 3/4 = ₹ 3,75,000, तथा रोहन की पूँजी = ₹ 5,00,000 × 1/4 = ₹ 1,25,000 होगी।

questions.text: नीता, विदुर तथा मीता एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 3:4:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। 1 अप्रैल, 2024 को उन्होंने समीर को एक नया साझेदार बनाने का निर्णय किया। नीता, विदुर, मीता तथा समीर का नया लाभ विभाजन अनुपात अब 1:1:1:1 होगा। समीर के प्रवेश से पूर्व नीता, विदुर तथा मीता का स्थिति विवरण मशीनरी का ₹ 6,00,000 का शेष दर्शा रहा था। प्रवेश की तिथि को यह पाया गया कि मशीनरी का मूल्यांकन 20% अधिक दर्शाया गया है। समीर के प्रवेश के बाद नये स्थिति विवरण में दर्शाया जाने वाला मशीनरी का मूल्य होगा :
questions.text_english: Nita, Vidur and Mita were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:4:1. On 1st April 2024, they decided to admit Samir as a new partner. The new profit sharing ratio between Nita, Vidur, Mita and Samir will now be 1:1:1:1. The balance sheet of Nita, Vidur and Mita before Samir's admission showed machinery at ₹ 6,00,000. On the date of admission, it was found that the machinery is overvalued by 20%. The value of machinery shown in the new Balance Sheet after Samir's admission will be:
questions.solution: The correct option is (D). The existing book value of the machinery is ₹ 6,00,000, which includes a 20% overvaluation. Let the true value of the machinery be 'x'. Thus, x + 20% of x = ₹ 6,00,000. This implies 1.20x = ₹ 6,00,000. Solving for x gives ₹ 6,00,000 / 1.20 = ₹ 5,00,000. The newly constituted firm will record the machinery at its correct true value in the new Balance Sheet, which is ₹ 5,00,000.
questions.solution_hindi: सही विकल्प (D) है। मशीनरी का वर्तमान पुस्तक मूल्य ₹ 6,00,000 है, जिसका मूल्यांकन 20% अधिक किया गया है। माना मशीनरी का सही मूल्य 'x' है, तो x + x का 20% = ₹ 6,00,000 होगा। 1.20x = ₹ 6,00,000. इसलिए x = ₹ 6,00,000 / 1.20 = ₹ 5,00,000. नई फर्म के स्थिति विवरण में मशीनरी इसके सही मूल्य ₹ 5,00,000 पर दिखाई जाएगी।

questions.text:
जैना, यश तथा किरण एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 2:2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। 1 जुलाई, 2024 को जैना की मृत्यु हो गयी। साझेदारी संलेख के अनुसार, जैना की मृत्यु की तिथि तक लाभ अथवा हानि में उसके भाग की गणना विक्रय के आधार पर की जायेगी। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष में विक्रय की राशि ₹ 4,00,000 तथा 1 अप्रैल से 30 जून, 2024 तक ₹ 1,50,000 थी। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए लाभ की गणना ₹ 1,00,000 की गयी। लेखा पुस्तकें प्रति वर्ष 31 मार्च को बंद की जाती हैं।
मृत्यु की तिथि तक फर्म के लाभ में जैना के भाग की गणना कीजिए तथा इसके लिये आवश्यक रोजनामचा प्रविष्टि कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
Zaina, Yash and Kiran were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio 2:2:1. Zaina died on 1st July, 2024. As per the partnership deed, Zaina's share of profit or loss till the date of her death was to be calculated on the basis of sales. Sales for the year ended 31st March, 2024 amounted to ₹ 4,00,000 and that from 1st April to 30th June, 2024 was ₹ 1,50,000. The profit for the year ending 31st March, 2024 was calculated as ₹ 1,00,000. The books of accounts are closed on 31st March every year.
Calculate Zaina's share of profit in the firm till the date of her death and pass necessary journal entry for the same.

key_points: Calculation of percentage of profit to sales for previous year: 25%
Calculation of firm's estimated profit till date of death: ₹ 37,500
Calculation of Zaina's share of profit: ₹ 15,000
Journal Entry debiting P&L Suspense A/c and crediting Zaina's Capital A/c with ₹ 15,000

questions.solution:
First, calculate the percentage of profit to sales for the previous year ending 31st March 2024. Profit was ₹ 1,00,000 on sales of ₹ 4,00,000, which gives a profit margin of 25% (1,00,000 / 4,00,000 × 100). Next, apply this margin to the sales from 1st April to 30th June 2024, which were ₹ 1,50,000. The estimated firm's profit till Zaina's death is 25% of ₹ 1,50,000, equaling ₹ 37,500. Zaina's share in this profit is calculated based on her profit-sharing ratio of 2/5. Therefore, Zaina's share is ₹ 37,500 × 2/5 = ₹ 15,000.

The necessary journal entry on 1st July, 2024 is:
Profit and Loss Suspense A/c  Dr.  ₹ 15,000
    To Zaina's Capital A/c                 ₹ 15,000

questions.text: रजत तथा करन की फर्म की पूँजी ₹ 15,00,000 है तथा ब्याज की बाज़ार दर 12% है। रजत तथा करन का वार्षिक वेतन क्रमशः ₹ 20,000 तथा ₹ 30,000 है। पिछले तीन वर्षों के लाभ क्रमशः ₹ 2,40,000, ₹ 2,80,000 तथा ₹ 3,20,000 थे। फ़र्म की ख्याति का मूल्यांकन पिछले तीन वर्षों के अधिलाभ के औसत के दो वर्षों के क्रय के आधार पर होगा। फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्यांकन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: The capital of the firm of Rajat and Karan is ₹ 15,00,000 and the market rate of interest is 12%. Annual salary of Rajat and Karan is ₹ 20,000 and ₹ 30,000 respectively. The profits for the last three years were ₹ 2,40,000, ₹ 2,80,000 and ₹ 3,20,000. Goodwill of the firm is to be valued on the basis of two years purchase of last three years' average super profits. Calculate the goodwill of the firm.

key_points: Calculate Normal Profit: ₹ 15,00,000 × 12% = ₹ 1,80,000
Deduct annual partners' salaries (₹ 50,000) to find Adjusted Average Profit: ₹ 2,30,000
Calculate Super Profit: ₹ 2,30,000 - ₹ 1,80,000 = ₹ 50,000
Calculate Goodwill: Super Profit (₹ 50,000) × 2 years = ₹ 1,00,000

questions.solution:
The valuation of goodwill based on super profits requires calculating both normal profit and adjusted average actual profit. The normal profit is derived by applying the market rate of interest (12%) to the capital employed (₹ 15,00,000), yielding ₹ 1,80,000. The average profit over the last three years is calculated by summing ₹ 2,40,000, ₹ 2,80,000, and ₹ 3,20,000 and dividing by 3, which results in ₹ 2,80,000. Since partners' salaries are standard business expenses, the total annual salary of ₹ 50,000 (Rajat ₹ 20,000 + Karan ₹ 30,000) is deducted from the average profit to determine the adjusted average actual profit, which is ₹ 2,30,000. 

The super profit is the excess of adjusted average actual profit over normal profit, equating to ₹ 50,000 (₹ 2,30,000 - ₹ 1,80,000). Finally, goodwill is calculated on the basis of two years' purchase of super profits: ₹ 50,000 × 2 = ₹ 1,00,000. Hence, the firm's goodwill is valued at ₹ 1,00,000.

questions.text_english:
Raja, Bharat and Vedika were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 2:2:1. Their Balance Sheet as on 31st March, 2024 was as follows:
[Balance Sheet Table in Image]
Vedika died on 31st July, 2024. According to the partnership deed, her legal representatives are entitled to the following:
(i) Balance in her capital account
(ii) Interest on capital @ 8% p.a.
(iii) Her share in the profit upto the date of death to be calculated on the basis of last year's profit. Vedika's share of profit was ₹ 3,000.
(iv) Her share of goodwill calculated on the basis of two years purchase of average profits of last three years. The average profit of last three years was ₹ 40,000. Vedika's drawings upto the date of death were ₹ 12,000.
Prepare Vedika's Capital Account to be rendered to her executors.

key_points: Opening balance (Credit): ₹ 90,000
Share of General Reserve (Credit): 1/5th of ₹ 50,000 = ₹ 10,000
Interest on capital (Credit): ₹ 90,000 × 8% × 4/12 = ₹ 2,400
Share of profit till death (Credit): ₹ 3,000
Share of goodwill (Credit): Total GW = 40,000 × 2 = 80,000. Share = 80,000 × 1/5 = 16,000 (Adjusted via Raja and Bharat)
Drawings (Debit): ₹ 12,000
Final balance transferred to Vedika's Executor's A/c: ₹ 1,09,400

questions.solution:
To prepare Vedika's Capital Account to be rendered to her executors, we meticulously post the required credits and debits as of the date of her death on 31st July 2024 (4 months into the financial year).

Vedika's Capital Account will be credited with her opening balance as per the Balance Sheet, which is ₹ 90,000. She is entitled to her 1/5th share of the General Reserve available on the Balance Sheet (₹ 50,000), which equals ₹ 10,000. Interest on her capital for 4 months is computed at 8% per annum on ₹ 90,000, contributing ₹ 2,400. Her predefined share in the profit till the date of death is given as ₹ 3,000. For goodwill, the firm's goodwill is valued at 2 years' purchase of the average profit of ₹ 40,000, amounting to ₹ 80,000. Vedika's 1/5th share is ₹ 16,000, which will be borne by the continuing partners (Raja and Bharat) in their gaining ratio, but recorded as a credit of ₹ 16,000 in her account.

On the debit side, Vedika's drawings during the period up to her death amount to ₹ 12,000. Summarizing these entries: total credits sum up to ₹ 1,21,400 (90,000 + 10,000 + 2,400 + 3,000 + 16,000) and the total debit is ₹ 12,000. The net balancing figure of ₹ 1,09,400 is transferred to Vedika's Executor's Account, representing the final amount payable to her legal heirs.

questions.text: पी एल लिमिटेड ₹ 10 प्रत्येक के 1,00,000 समता अंशों में विभक्त ₹ 10,00,000 की अधिकृत पूँजी के साथ पंजीकृत थी। कम्पनी ने जनता को अभिदान के लिए 90,000 समता अंश प्रस्तावित किये। 82,000 समता अंशों के लिए आवेदन प्राप्त हुए तथा सभी आवेदकों को अंशों का आबंटन कर दिया गया। अतिशय को आबंटित 2,000 अंशों पर, ₹ 2 प्रति अंश की प्रथम एवं अन्तिम याचना को छोड़कर, संपूर्ण देय राशि प्राप्त हो गयी। उसके अंशों का हरण कर लिया गया। निम्न प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए :
questions.text_english: PL Ltd. was registered with an authorised capital of ₹ 10,00,000 divided into 1,00,000 equity shares of ₹ 10 each. The company offered to the public for subscription 90,000 equity shares. Applications were received for 82,000 equity shares and shares were allotted to all the applicants. All money due was received with the exception of first and final call money of ₹ 2 per share on 2,000 shares allotted to Atishay. His shares were forfeited. Answer the following questions:

sub_questions.text: 'खातों की टिप्पणियों' में दर्शायी जाने वाली 'अदत्त याचना राशि' होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: The amount of 'Calls in Arrears' disclosed in 'Notes to Accounts' will be:
sub_questions.solution: The correct option is (C). Before forfeiture, the calls in arrears were ₹ 4,000 (2,000 shares × ₹ 2). However, once the shares are forfeited, the calls in arrears account is closed against the share capital account. Thus, in the Notes to Accounts reflecting the position after forfeiture, 'Calls in Arrears' will be nil.

sub_questions.text: हरण के पश्चात् पी एल लिमिटेड के अंशों की संख्या होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: The number of shares of PL Ltd. after forfeiture will be :
sub_questions.solution: The correct option is (D). The company received applications for and allotted 82,000 shares. Out of these, 2,000 shares held by Atishay were forfeited and have not yet been reissued. Therefore, the number of outstanding subscribed shares is 82,000 - 2,000 = 80,000.

sub_questions.text: 'खातों की टिप्पणियों' में 'अंश हरण खाते' के अन्तर्गत दर्शाई जाने वाली राशि होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: In the 'Notes to Accounts', the amount disclosed under 'Share Forfeiture Account' will be:

options.D: शून्य

sub_questions.solution: The correct option is (A). The Share Forfeiture Account holds the amount actually received on the forfeited shares. The face value is ₹ 10 and ₹ 2 was unpaid. Thus, the company had received ₹ 8 per share on Atishay's 2,000 shares. The amount transferred to the Forfeiture Account is 2,000 × ₹ 8 = ₹ 16,000.

sub_questions.text: 'खातों की टिप्पणियों' में 'निर्गमित पूँजी' के अंतर्गत दर्शाई जाने वाली राशि होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: In the 'Notes to Accounts', the amount disclosed under Issued Capital will be :
sub_questions.solution: The correct option is (B). Issued Capital refers to the nominal value of shares offered to the public for subscription by the company, regardless of the number of applications received. The company offered 90,000 equity shares of ₹ 10 each, so the issued capital is 90,000 × ₹ 10 = ₹ 9,00,000.

sub_questions.text: पी एल लिमिटेड के स्थिति विवरण में 'खातों के नोट्स' में 'अंश हरण खाते' के शेष को दर्शाया जायेगा :
sub_questions.text_english: Balance in 'Share Forfeiture Account' will be shown in 'Notes to Accounts' in the balance sheet of PL Ltd. under:

options.D: 'खातों के नोट्स' में नहीं दर्शाया जाएगा

options_english.D: Will not be shown in 'Notes to Accounts'

sub_questions.solution: The correct option is (C). As per Schedule III of the Companies Act, the balance of the Share Forfeiture Account (pertaining to shares not yet reissued) is added to the Paid-up Capital under the sub-head 'Subscribed Capital' in the Notes to Accounts forming part of the Balance Sheet.

sub_questions.text: पी एल लिमिटेड के स्थिति विवरण में दर्शायी जाने वाली 'अंश पूँजी' की राशि होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: The amount of 'Share Capital' disclosed in the balance sheet of PL Ltd. will be :
sub_questions.solution: The correct option is (B). After forfeiture, there are 80,000 subscribed and fully paid-up shares, yielding ₹ 8,00,000. The forfeited amount of ₹ 16,000 on the 2,000 shares is added to this. Therefore, the total amount disclosed as Share Capital on the face of the Balance Sheet is ₹ 8,00,000 + ₹ 16,000 = ₹ 8,16,000.

विभिन्न परिसम्पत्तियों (नगद को छोड़कर) तथा बाह्य देयताओं को वसूली खाते में हस्तांतरित करने के पश्चात् विभा तथा अजीत की साझेदारी फर्म के विघटन पर निम्नलिखित लेनदेनों की आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए :
(i) ₹ 46,000 के लेनदारों ने अपने दावें के पूर्ण निपटान में ₹ 9,000 नगद तथा ₹ 32,000 का फर्नीचर स्वीकार किया।
(ii) फर्म के पास ₹ 20,000 का स्टॉक था। अजीत ने 40% स्टॉक 10% बट्टे पर ले लिया जबकि शेष स्टॉक को ₹ 18,000 में बेचा गया।
(iii) विभा को विघटन कार्य की देखरेख के लिए नियुक्त किया गया जिसके लिए उसे ₹ 16,000 का वेतन देय था। विभा वसूली व्यय वहन करने के लिए सहमत हो गयी। ₹ 15,000 के वास्तविक वसूली व्ययों का भुगतान विभा ने किया।
(iv) ₹ 45,000 के अजीत के ऋण का निपटान ₹ 42,000 में किया गया।
(v) एक मशीन जिसका पुस्तकों में लेखा नहीं किया गया था, विभा ने ₹ 23,000 में ले ली, जबकि इसका संभावित मूल्य ₹ 28,000 था।
(vi) विघटन की तिथि को फर्म के लाभ-हानि खाते में ₹ 20,000 का नाम शेष था।
questions.text_english:
Pass the necessary journal entries for the following transactions on the dissolution of a partnership firm of Vibha and Ajit after various assets (other than cash) and external liabilities have been transferred to Realisation Account:
(i) Creditors worth ₹ 46,000 accepted ₹ 9,000 cash and furniture of ₹ 32,000 in full settlement of their claim.
(ii) The firm had stock of ₹ 20,000. Ajit took over 40% of the stock at a discount of 10% while the remaining stock was sold for ₹ 18,000.
(iii) Vibha was appointed to look after dissolution work for which she was allowed a remuneration of ₹ 16,000. Vibha agreed to bear the dissolution expenses. Actual dissolution expenses ₹ 15,000 were paid by Vibha.
(iv) Ajit's loan of ₹ 45,000 was settled at ₹ 42,000.
(v) A machine which was not recorded in the books was taken over by Vibha at ₹ 23,000, whereas its expected value was ₹ 28,000.
(vi) The firm had a debit balance of ₹ 20,000 in the Profit and Loss Account on the date of dissolution.

key_points: (i) Realisation A/c Dr 9,000 to Cash/Bank A/c 9,000 (No entry for asset taken by creditor).
(ii) Ajit's Capital Dr 7,200, Bank Dr 18,000 to Realisation A/c 25,200.
(iii) Realisation A/c Dr 16,000 to Vibha's Capital A/c 16,000 (No entry for actual expenses paid by partner out of own pocket).
(iv) Ajit's Loan A/c Dr 45,000 to Bank A/c 42,000, to Realisation A/c 3,000.
(v) Vibha's Capital A/c Dr 23,000 to Realisation A/c 23,000.
(vi) Vibha's Capital Dr, Ajit's Capital Dr to P&L A/c 20,000 (in their profit sharing ratio; if not given, assume equal 1:1, so 10,000 each).

questions.solution:
Here are the necessary journal entries in the books of the firm upon dissolution:

(i) Realisation A/c  Dr.  ₹ 9,000
      To Bank A/c                    ₹ 9,000
(Being cash paid to creditors in full settlement. No entry is required for the furniture taken over by creditors.)

(ii) Ajit's Capital A/c  Dr.  ₹ 7,200
     Bank A/c            Dr.  ₹ 18,000
       To Realisation A/c                ₹ 25,200
(Being 40% stock taken over by Ajit at 10% discount, i.e., ₹ 8,000 - ₹ 800 = ₹ 7,200, and remaining stock sold for ₹ 18,000)

(iii) Realisation A/c  Dr.  ₹ 16,000
        To Vibha's Capital A/c           ₹ 16,000
(Being remuneration allowed to Vibha. No entry is required for dissolution expenses since they were borne and paid personally by Vibha.)

(iv) Ajit's Loan A/c   Dr.  ₹ 45,000
        To Bank A/c                      ₹ 42,000
        To Realisation A/c               ₹ 3,000
(Being partner's loan settled and the gain of ₹ 3,000 credited to Realisation A/c)

(v) Vibha's Capital A/c  Dr.  ₹ 23,000
        To Realisation A/c               ₹ 23,000
(Being unrecorded asset taken over by Vibha at an agreed value of ₹ 23,000)

(vi) Assuming partners share profits and losses equally (1:1) as no ratio is given:
Vibha's Capital A/c  Dr.  ₹ 10,000
Ajit's Capital A/c   Dr.  ₹ 10,000
        To Profit & Loss A/c             ₹ 20,000
(Being accumulated loss distributed among partners).

आवेदन तथा आबंटन पर ₹ 7 प्रति अंश (₹ 1 प्रीमियम सहित)

sub_questions.text_english:
Altima Ltd. invited applications for issuing 2,00,000 equity shares of ₹ 10 each at a premium of ₹ 4 per share. The amount was payable as follows:
On application and allotment - ₹ 7 per share (including premium ₹ 1)
On first and final call - Balance
Applications were received for 2,40,000 shares. Applications for 30,000 shares were rejected and pro-rata allotment was made to the remaining applicants. Excess money received on application and allotment was returned. Manvi, who was allotted 4,000 shares failed to pay the first and final call money. Her shares were forfeited. All the forfeited shares were reissued at ₹ 4 per share fully paid up. Pass necessary journal entries in the books of Altima Ltd.

key_points: Receipt on application for 2,40k shares at ₹ 7 = 16,80k.

Allotment of 2,00k shares (Cap = 12,00k, SPR = 2,00k), Rejecting 30k shares (refund = 2,10k). Wait, applications = 240k. Reject 30k. Remaining 210k. Pro-rata for 200k. Excess is 10k shares × 7 = 70k. But text says 'Excess money received on application and allotment was returned'. Total refund = 40k shares × 7 = 2,80,000.
First & Final call due on 2,00k shares at ₹ 7 (₹ 4 Cap + ₹ 3 SPR) = 14,00,000.
Manvi fails to pay first & final call on 4,000 shares = 4,000 × 7 = 28,000.
Forfeiture entry: Share Cap Dr (4,000 × 10), SPR Dr (4,000 × 3) To Forfeited Shares (4,000 × 6), To Calls in Arrears (4,000 × 7).
Reissue entry: Bank Dr (4,000 × 4), Forfeited Shares Dr (4,000 × 6) To Share Cap (4,000 × 10).
Capital Reserve: Nil, since entire forfeited amount (24,000) was utilized for reissue discount.

sub_questions.solution:
Working Notes:
Issue size = 2,00,000 shares. Face Value = ₹ 10, Premium = ₹ 4.
Application & Allotment (₹ 7) = ₹ 6 Capital + ₹ 1 Premium.
First & Final Call (Balance) = ₹ 14 total issue price - ₹ 7 = ₹ 7 per share. This comprises ₹ 4 Capital and ₹ 3 Premium.
Applications received for 2,40,000 shares. Pro-rata made to 2,10,000 applicants for 2,00,000 shares, and 30,000 rejected. Excess money was completely returned, so refund is on (30,000 + 10,000) = 40,000 shares × ₹ 7 = ₹ 2,80,000.

Journal Entries in the books of Altima Ltd.:
1. Bank A/c                      Dr.  ₹ 16,80,000
     To Share App. & Allotment A/c          ₹ 16,80,000

2. Share App. & Allotment A/c    Dr.  ₹ 16,80,000
     To Share Capital A/c                   ₹ 12,00,000
     To Securities Premium A/c              ₹ 2,00,000
     To Bank A/c                            ₹ 2,80,000

3. Share First & Final Call A/c  Dr.  ₹ 14,00,000
     To Share Capital A/c                   ₹ 8,00,000
     To Securities Premium A/c              ₹ 6,00,000

4. Bank A/c                      Dr.  ₹ 13,72,000
   Calls-in-Arrears A/c          Dr.  ₹ 28,000
     To Share First & Final Call A/c        ₹ 14,00,000
(Call money received except on 4,000 shares of Manvi)

5. Share Capital A/c             Dr.  ₹ 40,000
   Securities Premium A/c        Dr.  ₹ 12,000
     To Share Forfeiture A/c                ₹ 24,000
     To Calls-in-Arrears A/c                ₹ 28,000
(Being 4,000 shares forfeited)

6. Bank A/c                      Dr.  ₹ 16,000
   Share Forfeiture A/c          Dr.  ₹ 24,000
     To Share Capital A/c                   ₹ 40,000
(Being forfeited shares reissued at ₹ 4 per share fully paid. Balance in Forfeiture A/c becomes nil, hence no transfer to Capital Reserve).

निम्न स्थितियों में अंशों के हरण तथा हरण किए गये अंशों के पुनः निर्गमन की आवश्यक रोजनामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए :
(i) मैसिल लिमिटेड ने ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 3,000 अंशों को जिन्हें 20% प्रीमियम पर निर्गमित किया गया था, ₹ 30 प्रति अंश की आबंटन राशि तथा ₹ 40 प्रति अंश (₹ 10 प्रीमियम सहित) की प्रथम याचना राशि का भुगतान न करने पर हरण कर लिया। ₹ 30 प्रति अंश (₹ 10 प्रीमियम सहित) की दूसरी तथा अंतिम याचना राशि अभी तक माँगी नहीं गयी थी। इनमें से 2,000 अंशों को ₹ 80 प्रति अंश प्रदत्त, ₹ 90 प्रति अंश में पुनः निर्गमित कर दिया गया।
(ii) एवियन लिमिटेड ने ₹ 10 प्रत्येक के उन 10,000 अंशों का हरण कर लिया जिन पर ₹ 4 प्रति अंश की प्रथम याचना प्राप्त नहीं हुई थी तथा ₹ 1 प्रति अंश की दूसरी तथा अन्तिम याचना अभी माँगी नहीं गयी थी। इनमें से 4,000 अंशों को ₹ 9 प्रति अंश पूर्ण प्रदत्त अजय को पुनः निर्गमित कर दिए गये।
sub_questions.text_english:
Pass necessary journal entries for forfeiture and reissue of forfeited shares in the following cases:
(i) Macil Ltd. forfeited 3,000 shares of ₹ 100 each issued at 20% premium for the non-payment of allotment money of ₹ 30 per share and first call of ₹ 40 per share (including premium ₹ 10). The second and final call of ₹ 30 per share (including premium ₹ 10) was not yet called. Out of these, 2,000 shares were reissued at ₹ 80 per share paid up for ₹ 90 per share.
(ii) Avian Ltd. forfeited 10,000 shares of ₹ 10 each on which the first call of ₹ 4 per share was not received and the second and final call of ₹ 1 per share was not yet called. Out of these, 4,000 shares were reissued to Ajay as fully paid up for ₹ 9 per share.

key_points: Case (i) Forfeiture: Called up capital = 100 - 20 (uncalled cap from final call) = 80 per share. Unpaid premium = 10 (allotment has no premium mentioned, assume premium on calls). Total premium = 20. Final call has 10, first call has 10. So allotment has no premium. Wait, if total premium is 20, and 1st call has 10 and 2nd call has 10, allotment has 0 premium. SPR Dr for 3000*10 = 30k.
Case (i) Reissue: Bank Dr 1,80k to Share Cap 1,60k, to SPR 20k.
Case (ii) Forfeiture: Called up capital = 9 per share. Share Cap Dr (10,000*9). Calls in Arrears (10,000*4). Share Forfeiture (10,000*5).
Case (ii) Reissue: Bank Dr 36k, Share Forfeiture Dr 4k To Share Cap 40k.

sub_questions.solution:
Journal Entries:

Case (i) Macil Ltd:
Total premium = 20%. Final call (uncalled) has ₹ 10 premium, First call has ₹ 10 premium. Hence, allotment has no premium. Called up capital per share = ₹ 100 - ₹ 20 (uncalled capital) = ₹ 80. Unpaid premium = ₹ 10 (from first call). Amount paid on application = ₹ 80 (called) + ₹ 10 (premium) - ₹ 30 (allot) - ₹ 40 (1st call) = ₹ 20 per share.
1. Share Capital A/c             Dr.  ₹ 2,40,000
   Securities Premium A/c        Dr.  ₹ 30,000
     To Share Forfeiture A/c                ₹ 60,000
     To Share Allotment A/c                 ₹ 90,000
     To Share First Call A/c                ₹ 120,000
(3,000 shares forfeited)

2. Bank A/c                      Dr.  ₹ 1,80,000
     To Share Capital A/c                   ₹ 1,60,000
     To Securities Premium A/c              ₹ 20,000
(2,000 shares reissued at ₹ 90 per share, ₹ 80 paid up)

3. Share Forfeiture A/c          Dr.  ₹ 40,000
     To Capital Reserve A/c                 ₹ 40,000
(Transfer of proportionate gain: ₹ 60,000/3000 × 2000 = ₹ 40,000)

Case (ii) Avian Ltd:
Called up capital = ₹ 10 - ₹ 1 (uncalled) = ₹ 9. Amount paid = ₹ 9 - ₹ 4 = ₹ 5.
4. Share Capital A/c             Dr.  ₹ 90,000
     To Share Forfeiture A/c                ₹ 50,000
     To Calls-in-Arrears (First Call)       ₹ 40,000
(10,000 shares forfeited)

5. Bank A/c                      Dr.  ₹ 36,000
   Share Forfeiture A/c          Dr.  ₹ 4,000
     To Share Capital A/c                   ₹ 40,000
(4,000 shares reissued to Ajay as fully paid up for ₹ 9)

6. Share Forfeiture A/c          Dr.  ₹ 16,000
     To Capital Reserve A/c                 ₹ 16,000
(Proportionate gain: ₹ 50,000/10000 × 4000 = ₹ 20,000. Less loss on reissue ₹ 4,000 = ₹ 16,000).

sub_questions.text:
आर्यन तथा आद्या एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 3:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। 31 मार्च, 2024 को उनका स्थिति विवरण निम्न प्रकार से था :
[Balance Sheet Table in Image]

(v) लेनदारों में सम्मिलित ₹ 3,500 की एक देयता के उत्पन्न होने की संभावना नहीं थी।

Aryan and Adya were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:1. Their Balance Sheet on 31st March, 2024 was as follows:
[Balance Sheet Table in Image]
Dev was admitted into the firm on 1st April, 2024 for 1/5th share in the profits of the firm on the following terms:
(i) Dev will bring capital proportionate to his share in the profits of the firm.
(ii) Goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹ 2,00,000 and Dev will bring his share of goodwill premium in cash.
(iii) Machinery was revalued at ₹ 4,50,000.
(iv) A provision for doubtful debts was to be created at 5% on debtors.
(v) A liability of ₹ 3,500 included in creditors was not likely to arise.
Prepare Revaluation Account and Partners' Capital Accounts on Dev's admission.

key_points: Revaluation Account: Credit side = Machinery (+60,000), Creditors (+3,500). Debit side = Provision for Doubtful Debts (+3,000 since 5% of 80,000 is 4,000, existing is 1,000, increase is 3,000). Gain = 60,500.
Distribution of Gain: Aryan (45,375) and Adya (15,125).
P&L A/c (Asset side) written off: Aryan Dr 15,000, Adya Dr 5,000.
WCR Distribution: Aryan Cr 15,000, Adya Cr 5,000.
Goodwill Premium brought by Dev: 1/5 of 2,00,000 = 40,000. Distributed to Aryan (30,000) and Adya (10,000).
Adjusted Capitals: Aryan = 3,95,375. Adya = 2,65,125. Total combined = 6,60,500.
Dev's Capital Calculation: 6,60,500 represents 4/5th share. Total Capital = 8,25,625. Dev's Capital = 1/5 of 8,25,625 = 1,65,125.

sub_questions.solution:
Revaluation Account:
Particulars                     Amount(₹)  Particulars                Amount(₹)
To Prov. for Doubtful Debts         3,000  By Machinery                  60,000
To Gain transferred to Cap A/cs:           By Creditors                   3,500
   Aryan (3/4)            45,375
   Adya (1/4)             15,125   60,500
Total                              63,500  Total                         63,500
(Note: Provision required is 5% of ₹ 80,000 = ₹ 4,000. Existing provision is ₹ 1,000. So, ₹ 3,000 more is created.)

Partners' Capital Accounts:
Aryan: Bal b/d ₹ 3,20,000; By WCR (3/4) ₹ 15,000; By Revaluation ₹ 45,375; By Premium for Goodwill ₹ 30,000; To P&L A/c (written off) ₹ 15,000. Closing Bal = ₹ 3,95,375.
Adya: Bal b/d ₹ 2,40,000; By WCR (1/4) ₹ 5,000; By Revaluation ₹ 15,125; By Premium for Goodwill ₹ 10,000; To P&L A/c (written off) ₹ 5,000. Closing Bal = ₹ 2,65,125.

Calculation of Dev's Capital:
Combined adjusted capital of Aryan and Adya = ₹ 3,95,375 + ₹ 2,65,125 = ₹ 6,60,500.
This represents their combined new share (1 - 1/5) = 4/5th of the total firm's capital.
Total firm's capital = ₹ 6,60,500 × 5/4 = ₹ 8,25,625.
Dev's capital (1/5th) = ₹ 8,25,625 × 1/5 = ₹ 1,65,125.

Dev's Capital Account:
By Bank A/c ₹ 1,65,125. Closing Bal = ₹ 1,65,125.

questions.text_english: The Debt Equity Ratio of Manak Enterprises is 2.5 : 1. Which of the following transaction will result in increase in this ratio ?

options.D: ₹ 4,00,000 पुस्तक मूल्य के फर्नीचर का 10% लाभ पर विक्रय।

questions.solution: The correct option is (C). The Debt to Equity ratio is Long-term Debt / Shareholders' Equity. The issue of debentures increases long-term debt while keeping equity constant, thus mathematically increasing the ratio. Option A and B affect current liabilities and current assets, leaving long-term debt and equity unchanged. Option D increases equity (due to the profit on sale), which would decrease the ratio.

key_points: Let Credit Purchase be x. Cash Purchase = 0.25x.
Total Purchase = 1.25x = 15,00,000. So, Credit Purchase (x) = 12,00,000.
Average Trade Payables = Net Credit Purchases / Trade Payables Turnover Ratio = 12,00,000 / 4 = 3,00,000.
Let Opening Trade Payables be y. Closing Trade Payables = 2y.
Average Trade Payables = (y + 2y) / 2 = 1.5y.
1.5y = 3,00,000, therefore Opening Trade Payables (y) = 2,00,000.
Closing Trade Payables = 2 × 2,00,000 = 4,00,000.

sub_questions.solution:
Let Credit Purchases be x. Since cash purchases are 25% of credit purchases, Cash Purchases = 0.25x. The total purchases amount to ₹ 15,00,000, so the equation is: x + 0.25x = ₹ 15,00,000. Solving this gives 1.25x = ₹ 15,00,000, which means Credit Purchases (x) = ₹ 12,00,000.

The Trade Payables Turnover Ratio is calculated as Net Credit Purchases divided by Average Trade Payables. Using the given ratio of 4 times: ₹ 12,00,000 / Average Trade Payables = 4. This implies Average Trade Payables = ₹ 3,00,000.

Let Opening Trade Payables be y. The problem states Closing Trade Payables are twice the opening, so they are 2y. The formula for average trade payables is (Opening + Closing)/2. Thus, (y + 2y)/2 = ₹ 3,00,000. This simplifies to 1.5y = ₹ 3,00,000. Solving for y gives ₹ 2,00,000. 
Therefore, Opening Trade Payables are ₹ 2,00,000 and Closing Trade Payables are ₹ 4,00,000.

First, calculate Capital Employed using the liabilities approach: Shareholders Funds + Non-Current Liabilities (10% Debentures) = ₹ 16,00,000 + ₹ 8,00,000 = ₹ 24,00,000.
Next, calculate EBIT. The Net Profit After Tax is ₹ 3,00,000, and Tax is ₹ 1,00,000. Hence, Net Profit Before Tax is ₹ 4,00,000. We must add back the interest on long-term debt to find EBIT. Interest on the 10% Debentures of ₹ 8,00,000 is ₹ 80,000. So, EBIT = ₹ 4,00,000 + ₹ 80,000 = ₹ 4,80,000.

Now, apply the ROI formula: (₹ 4,80,000 / ₹ 24,00,000) × 100. This yields 20%. Therefore, the Return on Investment is 20%.

key_points: Machine sold: Book Value = 50,000 - 20,000 = 30,000. Sale Value = 30,000 + 10% profit = 33,000 (Inflow).
Machinery Account: Opening balance 3,00,000. Less cost of machine sold 50,000 = 2,50,000. Closing balance is 3,80,000. So, purchase of Machinery = 1,30,000 (Outflow).
Net Cash Used in Investing Activities = 33,000 (Inflow) - 1,30,000 (Outflow) = (97,000).

sub_questions.solution:
First, calculate the sale proceeds of the machinery. The book value of the machine sold is ₹ 50,000 (cost) - ₹ 20,000 (accumulated depreciation) = ₹ 30,000. It was sold at a 10% profit, meaning the profit is ₹ 3,000. Thus, the cash inflow from the sale of machinery is ₹ 30,000 + ₹ 3,000 = ₹ 33,000.

Next, determine the purchase of machinery by preparing a Machinery Account at cost. The opening balance is ₹ 3,00,000. The cost of the machine sold, ₹ 50,000, is credited to the account. To achieve the closing balance of ₹ 3,80,000, there must be a balancing figure on the debit side, representing the purchase of new machinery. Purchase = ₹ 3,80,000 + ₹ 50,000 - ₹ 3,00,000 = ₹ 1,30,000 (Outflow).

The Net Cash Flow from Investing Activities is the difference between inflows and outflows. It equals ₹ 33,000 (Sale) - ₹ 1,30,000 (Purchase) = (₹ 97,000). Thus, cash used in investing activities is ₹ 97,000.

To calculate cash flows from financing activities, we analyze the changes in equity and long-term liabilities. 

Equity Share Capital increased from ₹ 8,00,000 to ₹ 12,00,000, indicating an issue of shares generating a cash inflow of ₹ 4,00,000. Alongside this, Securities Premium increased from ₹ 1,00,000 to ₹ 1,40,000, representing a premium of ₹ 40,000 received on the issue of these shares. Summarizing the net effect: ₹ 4,40,000 (Inflow from Shares) - ₹ 1,00,000 (Redemption of Debentures) - ₹ 40,000 (Interest Paid) = ₹ 3,00,000. Therefore, the net cash inflow from financing activities is ₹ 3,00,000.

questions.text_english: What is meant by 'Data', 'Information' and 'Transaction'?

key_points: Data refers to raw, unprocessed facts, figures, and details.
Information is processed, organised, and structured data that provides meaningful context and aids in decision-making.
Transaction is an economic event or business activity that involves the exchange of values and impacts the financial position of the business.

questions.solution:
Data refers to the raw, unorganized, and unprocessed facts, figures, or observations that lack specific meaning in isolation. It serves as the basic input for any processing system. 

Information is data that has been processed, structured, and presented in a meaningful and useful context, enabling management and users to make informed decisions.

A Transaction is a specific economic event or business activity entered into by a firm that involves an exchange of money, goods, or services, and which objectively alters the financial state of the business, requiring a record in the books of accounts.

Six key features of an Accounting Software include:
1. Speed and Accuracy: It processes vast amounts of numerical data rapidly and eliminates human mathematical errors.
2. Automated Document Production: It can automatically generate essential documents like invoices, receipts, and account statements.
3. Real-time Updating: Entering a transaction instantly updates all related ledgers and financial statements without manual posting.
4. Scalability: It can easily accommodate a growing volume of business transactions without proportionally increasing the administrative burden.
5. Security and Access Control: It offers robust data protection through password controls, user permissions, and encryption.
6. Flexible Reporting: It allows users to quickly generate diverse, customized, and comparative financial reports at any time.

key_points: Text Data: Contains alphanumeric characters used for labels and descriptions.
Number Data: Numeric values used for mathematical calculations.
Date and Time Data: Values formatted specifically to represent dates and times, which can be manipulated chronologically.
Formula Data: Mathematical expressions or functions used to calculate results based on other cells.

sub_questions.solution:
An Excel worksheet generally accommodates four primary types of data within its cells:
1. Text (Labels): This includes alphabetic characters, symbols, or alphanumeric combinations that are generally used for headings, names, or descriptive data that is not subjected to mathematical calculations.
2. Numbers (Values): These are purely numeric entries (including decimals) that Excel recognizes as quantities, allowing users to perform arithmetic operations on them.
3. Dates and Times: Although stored internally as serial numbers, these are specific data types formatted to represent dates and times, allowing for chronological calculations and filtering.
4. Formulas/Functions: These are mathematical equations or built-in functions starting with an equal sign (=). They do not represent static data but dynamically calculate and display a result based on values stored in other cells.

Data Validation is a crucial feature in Excel designed to restrict the type, format, or values of data that a user can enter into a specific cell. It acts as a preventative control to ensure data consistency and accuracy, such as restricting input to a specific date range, a whole number, or a dropdown list of pre-approved items.

It allows the designer to define the exact response the system should give when a user attempts to input invalid data. It provides three styles of alerts: 'Stop' (prevents the invalid entry entirely), 'Warning' (warns the user but allows them to proceed), and 'Information' (simply informs the user).
